questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Power of biconvex lens is $P$ diopter. When it is cut into two symmetrical halves by a plane containing the principal axis. The ratio of power of two halves is
questions.solution:
Power of equiconvex lens $=P$
i.e $P=\frac{1}{f}$, where $f$ is focal length of equiconvex lens.
When an equiconvex lens is cut into two symmetrical halves by a plane containing the principal axis, then its focal length remains same.
Hence, power of lens (each halves)
$\begin{aligned}
& P^{\prime}=\frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow P^{\prime}=P \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{P^{\prime}}{P}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad P: P=1: 1
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In normal adjustment, for a refracting telescope, the distance between objective and eye piece is 30 cm . The focal length of the objective, when the angular magnification of the telescope is 2 , will be:
questions.solution:
$\because \mathrm{f}_0+\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{e}}=30$
And magnification, $\mathrm{m}=\frac{\mathrm{f}_0}{\mathrm{f}_e}2=\frac{\mathrm{f}_0}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{e}}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}_0=2 \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{e}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}_0+\frac{\mathrm{f}_0}{2}=30 \therefore \mathrm{f}_0=20cm$

questions.q: If the distance between object and its two times magnified virtual image produced by a curved mirror is 15 cm , the focal length of the mirror must be:
questions.solution: Since, image is magnified. So, it is a concave mirror. $\therefore \mathrm{m}=2=\frac{-\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}2=\frac{-(15-u)}{-u}2 u=15-u3 \mathrm{u}=15 \Rightarrow \mathrm{u}=5 \mathrm{~cm}\mathrm{v}=15-\mathrm{u}=15-5=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ Bymirror formula, $\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{(-5)}=\frac{1-2}{10}=\frac{-1}{10}\mathrm{f}=-10 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin prism $P_1$ with an angle $6^{\circ}$ and made of glass of refractive index 1.54 is combined with another prism $\mathrm{P}_2$ made from glass of refractive index 1.72 to produce dispersion without average deviation. The angle of prism $\mathrm{P}_2$ is :
questions.solution:
Angle of deviation for first prism
$\delta_1=A_1\left(\mu_1-1\right)=6(1.54-1)$
Angle of deviation for second prism
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \delta_2=A_2\left(\mu_2-1\right) \\ \\ & =A_2(1.72-1) \\ \end{aligned}$
For dispersion without deviation
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \delta_1=\delta_2 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 6^{\circ}(1.54-1)=\mathrm{A}_2(1.72-1) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{A}_2=\frac{6^{\circ} \times 0.54}{0.72}=\frac{18^{\circ}}{4}=4.5^{\circ} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a reflecting telescope, a secondary mirror is used to:
options: reduce the problem of mechanical support
move the eyepiece outside the telescopic tube
questions.solution:
(d) To redirect the light that enters the telescope to the eyepiece or camera. The primary mirror of a reflecting telescopes gathers the light and reflects towards the secondary mirror which then reflect the light towards the eyepiece allowing the observer to see image.
It has advantage of a large focal length in a short telescope.

questions.solution:
For the given convex lens, focal length, f=25 cm

Magnification of lens in terms of u and f is given by,

m=ff+u=2525+u        ...i

When the image is real, then m=-2 and u=-x1

∴ From Eq. (i), -2=2525-x1⇒x1=752

Again, when the image is virtual, then m=2 and u=-x2

∴ From Eq. (i), 2=2525-x2⇒x2=252

Hence, the ratio of x2 and x1 is

∴ x2x1=25/275/2=13

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The focal length of a thin convex lens for red and blue rays are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>96</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> respectively. Then, the dispersive power of the material of the lens is
questions.solution:
Dispersive power is ratio of angular dispersion and mean deviation.

It can be written in terms of focal length as,

ω=fr-fbfy

Here fr=100 cm

fb=96.8 cm

fy=fb×fr

=96.8×100

≈98.34 cm

∴ Dispersive power

ω=fr-fbfy

=100-96.898.34

≈0.0325
Hence, the dispersive power of the material of the lens is 0.0325.

If lenses are made of different materials of refractive indices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></math> is the radius of curvature of the curved surface of the lenses, then the focal length of combination is
questions.solution:
Focal length of combination

1f=1f1+1f2    …i

Using lens maker's formula 
1f2=μ2-11-R-1∞=-μ2-1R

1f1=μ1-11∞-1-R=μ1-1R

or 1f1=μ1-1R

1f2=-μ2-1R

Putting these values in Equation (i), we get

⇒ 1f=μ1-1R-μ2-1R

⇒ 1f=μ1-1-μ2+1R

⇒ 1f=μ1-μ2R

f=Rμ1-μ2
